# CREATE SOMETHING Draw

CREATE SOMETHING Draw is a free, local-first drawing canvas for mapping meetings and spatial notes.

## Capabilities

- Draw free-form pen strokes, rectangles, ellipses, and arrows.
- Add editable spatial notes and organize work with groups.
- Convert selected marks into notes, connectors, or groups while retaining source provenance.
- Export the canvas as JSON, SVG, or PNG and import compatible JSON documents.
- Control the visible canvas with sixteen WebMCP site tools in supported agent browsers.

## Agent interface

Draw registers a semantic WebMCP surface through `document.modelContext.registerTool`: compact inspection, composition, paths, partial patches, layout, camera focus, targeted revert, dedicated destructive actions, complete state, low-level operations, selection, tool choice, history, and reset. Agent changes use the same local document, history, and persistence operations as human changes, return revision-bearing receipts, and display an on-canvas transition. WebMCP mutation is limited to the browser-local canvas; paired native shells use their dedicated synchronization controls.

## Data boundary

Canvas content is saved only on the current device in browser storage. CREATE SOMETHING does not receive the canvas contents. Browser storage and installed-app state are specific to the hostname in use, so use JSON export and import when moving between origins or devices.

## Canonical URL

https://draw.createsomething.agency/

## Mac pilot 0.1.1

https://draw.createsomething.agency/download

Draw 0.1.1 for Apple Silicon, macOS 13 or later, is Developer ID signed, Apple notarized, stapled and Gatekeeper accepted. Pilot delivery is by request; no public binary is hosted yet. The landing page records the exact application source revision and DMG checksum. Physical iPhone pairing and Intel compatibility are not qualified for this pilot. Notes support block hierarchy, lists, quotes and selected emphasis. JSON is the editable backup and handoff format; SVG and PNG are presentation exports. Browser agent mutations remain browser-local and are unavailable in paired native shells.
